summary: Streaming reconnect in Go SDK causes duplicate tool/function invocations when connection lost
description: Customer reports that when their Go-based service loses a streaming connection to the Redwood API (intermittent network blips), the SDK reconnects but their backend tools (webhook-style function calls) are executed twice. The customer is using the Go SDK with an on-message 'tool' execution flow: the model issues a tool call and the SDK relays that to their internal tool runner. After a reconnect, the same tool invocation appears again, leading to duplicate downstream side effects (order creation, email sends).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use the Go SDK to open a streaming chat session with a tool/call function handler registered on the customer's side.
2) Have the model issue a tool call that results in an outbound POST from customer's relay to internal tool-runner (single-shot operation, non-idempotent on their side).
3) Simulate a transient network drop between client and Redwood streaming endpoint (TCP connection reset or short firewall rule blocking ~2s).
4) Observe that the Go SDK reconnects/reauthorizes and the model's tool call is delivered again; the customer's tool-runner receives a duplicate POST and performs the action twice.
5) Reproduce consistently when reconnect occurs before explicit SDK acknowledgement/receipt confirmation logic is added client-side.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-01 - Initial triage by Support: customer not using explicit idempotency key on tool payloads; Go SDK default streaming reconnect path issues a fresh request without preserved idempotency metadata.

2026-03-01 - Confirmed behavior with local repro using network emulator: when reconnection occurs before SDK had a chance to persist/ack the prior tool event, the runtime re-emits tool_call tokens and the SDK forwards them as new invocations.

2026-03-01 - Hypothesis: SDK does not automatically attach or persist an 'Idempotency-Key' across streaming reconnects for server-emitted tool calls. Reconnects are treated as new events and the customer's tool-runner receives the same invocation twice.
2026-03-01 - Related internal issue INT-4210 tracks improving SDK reconnect semantics and adding opt-in persistent idempotency for streaming tool events.

2026-03-02 - Engineering note: serving-runtime currently does not dedupe tool_call events by invocation_id across separate HTTP sessions; dedupe responsibility left to clients using idempotency keys or tracking invocation IDs.
2026-03-02 - Temporary reproduction script attached in customer's environment; shows duplicate POSTs with identical invocation_id in payload but no idempotency header.
comments: Support (Aisha): Can you confirm whether you set an idempotency key or invocation_id on the tool payload? If not, please try adding one and re-testing. Also share the Go SDK minor version (go.mod) and the exact streaming call pattern.

Customer (MarketFlow Engineers): We're on sdk-go v0.8.3. We don't set a separate idempotency header today; we relied on the SDK to avoid replaying tool events. Attaching minimal repro code. We can add an invocation_id but concerned about losing dedupe if the SDK rewrites headers on reconnect.

Support (Aisha): Thanks — we reproduced locally. Filing to Eng. For immediate mitigation: either (A) add a unique invocation_id field inside the tool payload and make your tool-runner reject duplicates, or (B) disable automatic reconnects in the SDK and implement a single-flight ack on your side. Both are supported workarounds.

Eng (Liam): We'll prepare a patch to the Go SDK to preserve Idempotency-Key across reconnects and add a streaming option to opt-in to "persisted-idempotency" semantics. Opening PR referenced above. Investigation continues for server-side dedupe improvements.
Customer: We'll apply an invocation_id-based dedupe as a short-term fix and test the SDK patch once available.
resolution: Workaround applied by customer: they added an invocation_id inside the tool payload and updated their tool-runner to ignore duplicate invocation_ids. Engineering (SDK) will ship a fix: SDK change to persist provided Idempotency-Key and to expose a WithPersistedIdempotency(true) option for streaming sessions. PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/912 contains the patch; rollout planned to 0.8.5. Also updating docs: recommend always supplying an idempotency key or invocation_id for non-idempotent tool side effects.
resolution_notes: Patch in PR 912: preserve Idempotency-Key header across reconnects; add option to enable persisted idempotency on streaming sessions.
Docs updated: Streaming best-practices page — explicit idempotency for tool calls and sample Go/TS snippets.
Customer verification: MarketFlow ran a 24h soak test and observed no duplicate tool executions after adding invocation_id dedupe and testing #912 in a staging environment.
Rollout plan: Canary release of SDK 0.8.5 to selected customers next week, full release two weeks after canary if no regressions.
Follow-up: Evaluate server-side dedupe for tool_call invocation_id in serving-runtime (tracked in INT-4210).
attachments_description: Contains minimal Go repro and connection trace logs demonstrating duplicate POSTs to customer's tool-runner.
customer_impact: Duplicate external side effects for non-idempotent operations (orders, emails). Customer considers this high-impact and is on enterprise SLA.
next_steps: 1) Eng to review and merge PR 912 for SDK patch (assigned: Liam).
2) Release SDK 0.8.5 with canary + release notes about idempotency and streaming reconnects.
3) Support to follow up with customer after canary deployment and assist with testing.
4) Track server-side dedupe feasibility in INT-4210 and report back in 2 weeks.
